title: Everwyn
summary: An overview of Everwyn, its geography, regions, and the civilizations that inhabit the known world.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Everwyn is the known world, encompassing the lands, kingdoms, and territories inhabited by its many peoples. Its history and geography have shaped the rise and fall of civilizations, the formation of political powers, and the spread of religious traditions.

sections.heading: Geography
paragraphs: The lands of Everwyn are divided into distinct regions, each with its own landscapes, settlements, and resources. Mountains, forests, rivers, and fertile territories influence the boundaries and relationships between neighboring kingdoms.

sections.heading: Political Divisions
paragraphs: Everwyn is home to numerous kingdoms and factions, each pursuing its own interests and ambitions. Their relationships are shaped by territorial disputes, alliances, inherited authority, and the influence of the Council of the Seven.

title: The Divine Order
summary: The divine hierarchy governing the relationship between the gods, the mortal world, and the forces that shape existence.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Divine Order is the established structure of divine authority and the relationship between the gods and the world of mortals. Its existence influences religious institutions, cultural traditions, and the understanding of power throughout Everwyn.

sections.heading: Divine Authority
paragraphs: The gods occupy positions of extraordinary authority within the established order. Their influence extends beyond worship, shaping the beliefs, customs, and institutions of mortal civilizations.

sections.heading: The Nature of Divinity
paragraphs: The nature and limitations of divine power remain subjects of religious and philosophical debate. Questions surrounding the mortality, legitimacy, and succession of the gods challenge the assumptions upon which the Divine Order rests.

sections.heading: The Threat of Deicide
paragraphs: The possibility of killing a god represents a fundamental challenge to the established divine hierarchy. Any attempt to destroy or replace a deity threatens not only religious institutions, but the balance of power between the divine and mortal worlds.

title: The First Reign (0–78)
summary: The beginning of recorded history in Everwyn, marked by the rise of the First King and the establishment of a unified kingdom.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The First Reign marks the beginning of recorded history in Everwyn. During this period, the First King established his authority over the territories and brought the entirety of Everwyn under a single crown.
His reign saw the establishment of a centralized monarchy, the creation of royal institutions, and the introduction of unified laws and administrative systems.

sections.heading: The Rise of the First King
paragraphs: The emergence of the first recognized monarch of Everwyn, whose military campaigns and political influence brought the territories under his authority.

sections.heading: The Unification of Everwyn
paragraphs: The consolidation of the seven territories into a single kingdom under the rule of the First King, ending the period of independent regional governance.

sections.heading: The Royal Proclamation
paragraphs: The formal declaration of the unified Kingdom of Everwyn, establishing the First King as its sovereign ruler and introducing the principles of centralized royal authority.

sections.heading: The Establishment of the Royal Court
paragraphs: The creation of the royal administration, including the appointment of noble advisors, ministers, magistrates, and other officials responsible for governing the kingdom.

sections.heading: The Founding of the Capital
paragraphs: The establishment of the kingdom's capital as the political, administrative, and cultural center of Everwyn. The city became the seat of the monarchy and the location of the royal palace.

title: The Kingdom of Everwyn (78–200)
summary: The continuation of the unified monarchy following the First King's reign, characterized by political consolidation, economic expansion, and institutional development.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Following the First King's reign, Everwyn continued under a unified monarchy. This period was characterized by political consolidation, economic expansion, and the development of institutions that would govern the kingdom for generations.
The royal government invested heavily in infrastructure, education, and commerce, connecting distant settlements and encouraging the growth of a shared national identity.

sections.heading: The Royal Succession
paragraphs: The transfer of the crown following the end of the First King's reign, establishing the hereditary succession of the monarchy and ensuring the continuation of the unified kingdom.

sections.heading: The Expansion of the Kingdom
paragraphs: A period of territorial and economic growth during which the monarchy extended its influence into previously undeveloped settlements and established new administrative districts throughout Everwyn.

sections.heading: The Establishment of the Royal Academy
paragraphs: The founding of a prestigious institution dedicated to higher education, scholarship, magical studies, and the advancement of the arts and sciences. The academy became an important center of intellectual and cultural development.

sections.heading: The Great Royal Census
paragraphs: The first comprehensive census of the kingdom's population, land, and resources. The undertaking provided the monarchy with detailed records of its territories and established a standardized system of taxation and civil administration.

sections.heading: The Construction of the King's Highway
paragraphs: The development of an extensive network of roads connecting the capital to the kingdom's major settlements. The highway facilitated trade, travel, military transportation, and communication between distant territories.

title: The Age of Fracture (200–225)
summary: The collapse of the unified Kingdom of Everwyn and the establishment of seven independent territories.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Age of Fracture began with the death of the First King and the subsequent destabilization of the unified monarchy. Disagreements over royal succession, regional autonomy, and political authority weakened the central government, resulting in growing tensions between the royal court and regional leadership.

Following years of political unrest, the former kingdom dissolved into seven independent territories. The period concluded with the formal recognition of the Seven Regions and the establishment of their respective governments.

sections.heading: The Death of the First King
paragraphs: The death of Everwyn's founding monarch, marking the beginning of a period of political instability and uncertainty surrounding the future of the unified kingdom.

sections.heading: The Succession Crisis
paragraphs: A prolonged political dispute concerning the inheritance of the royal crown. Competing claims to the throne, disagreements among the nobility, and growing regional dissatisfaction weakened the authority of the monarchy.

sections.heading: The Dissolution of the Royal Court
paragraphs: The gradual collapse of the centralized royal administration as regional governors and noble houses withdrew their allegiance to the monarchy. Former royal institutions were divided, abandoned, or reorganized under emerging regional authorities.

sections.heading: The Sevenfold Division
paragraphs: The formal dissolution of the Kingdom of Everwyn and the establishment of seven independent regions. Former territorial boundaries were reorganized into [[argentum]], [[aurun]], [[cupri]], [[galena]], [[ferron]], [[mercurium]], and [[plata]].

sections.heading: The Treaty of Seven Crowns
paragraphs: A diplomatic agreement recognizing the sovereignty of the Seven Regions and establishing the foundations for peaceful relations between their respective governments. The treaty addressed territorial boundaries, political recognition, and the rights of regional rulers.

title: The Age of Seven Crowns (225–500)
summary: The development of the Seven Regions following the dissolution of the unified kingdom, establishing the political and cultural foundations of modern Everwyn.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Following the dissolution of the unified kingdom, the Seven Regions entered a period of political and cultural development. Each territory established its own government, legal institutions, and ruling authority, gradually developing the regional identities recognized throughout modern Everwyn.

Although the early centuries were marked by territorial disputes and competing political interests, the period also saw significant advancements in commerce, architecture, education, and regional diplomacy. The development of independent governments established the political foundations of contemporary Everwyn.

sections.heading: The Founding of the Seven Regions
paragraphs: Following the Sevenfold Division, the former territories formally established themselves as independent regions: [[argentum]], [[aurun]], [[cupri]], [[galena]], [[ferron]], [[mercurium]], and [[plata]]. Each developed its own ruling authority, administrative institutions, and regional capital, marking the beginning of the Seven Crowns.

sections.heading: The War of Seven Banners
paragraphs: A major military conflict involving several of the Seven Regions over disputed territories, political influence, and regional sovereignty. The conflict resulted in significant territorial changes and prompted renewed diplomatic negotiations between the regional governments.

sections.heading: The First Interregional Treaty
paragraphs: An agreement between the Seven Regions establishing formal diplomatic relations and guidelines for international commerce, travel, and the peaceful resolution of territorial disputes. The treaty laid the foundations for long-term cooperation and international relations.

sections.heading: The Rise of Regional Institutions
paragraphs: A period of significant political, economic, and cultural development during which the Seven Regions established their own educational institutions, commercial guilds, legal systems, and administrative organizations. These developments contributed to the growth of regional identities and the expansion of interregional commerce.

title: The Age of Embers (500–Present)
summary: The current historical period of Everwyn, characterized by relative peace, economic prosperity, technological advancement, and increased cooperation between the Seven Regions.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Age of Embers is the current historical period of Everwyn, characterized by relative peace, economic prosperity, technological advancement, and increased cooperation between the Seven Regions.

Following centuries of political consolidation and regional development, Everwyn entered an era of unprecedented cultural and commercial growth. Improvements in transportation, education, agriculture, and manufacturing contributed to the expansion of regional economies, while diplomatic agreements strengthened relationships between the independent territories.

sections.heading: The Long Winter
paragraphs: An unusually severe winter that prompted the development of improved agricultural storage, heating systems, and regional emergency provisions. Its legacy contributed to greater cooperation between the regions.

sections.heading: The Founding of the Grand Academy
paragraphs: The establishment of a prominent institution dedicated to scholarship, magical research, and the advancement of the arts and sciences.

sections.heading: The Modern Trade Accords
paragraphs: A series of commercial agreements that standardized trade regulations, reduced tariffs, and encouraged economic cooperation between the regions.

sections.heading: The Era of Invention
paragraphs: A period of rapid technological development marked by improvements in transportation, communication, manufacturing, and everyday conveniences.
